reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily provides instructional guidance for contacting Instagram through in-app reporting, the Help Center, Facebook, and Twitter about account and feature problems. The frames show Instagram support menus and Help Center pages, and the request to subscribe is described as ordinary audience engagement rather than a financial or data-related condition. A separate mention of free training about making money through an external website does not establish its terms, operator, costs, outcomes, or any information or payment request.

citations.quote: I wanted to make this video to show you a few places where you could contact Instagram.
under support that says report a problem
the Instagram Help Center could be helpful from time to time
But this is another way to do it. And the last one is using Twitter.

opening.argument: The video does more than explain Instagram support: it pairs an income promise with a concrete viewer action. The description tells viewers to “Check out the free training” that is said to explain how to “make money on Instagram,” then directs them to an external website. That is a low-friction pathway from viewing the video to pursuing a promised financial benefit, even though the material does not explain the training’s operator, conditions, or how the claimed income would be achieved. The surrounding support tutorial can make that call to action appear more trustworthy, but it does not clarify the offer itself.

citations.quote: Check out the free training on how to get more followers and make money on Instagram @ www.howfinitycourse.com
Please leave any questions on the comment section and hopefully someone can answer it.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference argument treats the external training as incidental, but the description explicitly directs viewers to it and connects it to making money on Instagram. Calling it “free” does not establish what later participation may require, and ordinary comments or subscriptions do not explain why an income-oriented external destination is included alongside the tutorial. The support instructions therefore do not resolve the separate solicitation.

citations.quote: Check out the free training on how to get more followers and make money on Instagram @ www.howfinitycourse.com
please make sure you subscribe to this channel

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited wording establishes only that free training is advertised; it does not establish deception, payment, data collection, an unusually easy reward, or any required action beyond checking the website. “Make money” is a broad topic claim, not a guaranteed return. The bulk of the material remains practical support guidance, including reporting a problem and using the Help Center.

citations.quote: Check out the free training on how to get more followers and make money on Instagram @ www.howfinitycourse.com

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: an external website, an explicitly income-oriented training offer, and branding for the same creator visible throughout the support demonstrations. The description places the external destination immediately after instructions to seek help and invites viewers into a training that promises to help them make money on Instagram. That combination can steer viewers from a credible-looking platform tutorial toward an unexamined financial opportunity. The supplied material gives no terms, eligibility requirements, operator details, or evidence supporting the income claim, so the offer is presented with substantial unanswered risk.

citations.quote: Check out the free training on how to get more followers and make money on Instagram @ www.howfinitycourse.com
I've made close to a hundred Instagram videos on this YouTube channel.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference side focuses on the visible support screens, but those screens do not eliminate the external income promotion. The description itself supplies the relevant risk signal: a money-making claim paired with a website. The fact that the training is called free addresses only an initial price, not the offer’s terms or whether viewers are later steered into something else.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are contextual concerns, not proof of a scam category. The material does not show a guaranteed return, urgency, payment request, investment, recruitment structure, or harmful outcome. The external training is expressly described as free, while the demonstrated content explains ordinary support routes and acknowledges that Instagram may not respond.

opening.argument: Although the video presents itself as technical help, its broader structure also functions as audience-building promotion. The speaker emphasizes having nearly a hundred Instagram videos, invites viewers to use the comment section and subscribe, and the description adds a free training link about getting followers and making money. The support walkthrough supplies useful subject matter, but it also establishes authority and draws viewers toward the creator’s other materials and external site. In that context, the income-training invitation is not merely an unrelated aside; it is part of a promotional funnel attached to the instructional presentation.

The support tutorial’s apparent usefulness may increase trust in the creator without providing any substantiation for the separate income opportunity.
